candidate_facts.name: Tantalum
candidate_facts.sample: Johnson, Matthey & Co., Ltd., London sample, vacuum-annealed at NBS
candidate_facts.sample_locator: Section 2.13 Tantalum (Cubic), printed p. 29 / PDF p. 33: Johnson, Matthey sample, dissolved gases and hydride, vacuum annealing, trace impurities and body-centered cubic structure.
candidate_facts.density_locator: Section 2.13 continued, printed p. 31 / PDF p. 35, upper left: density calculated from the NBS lattice constant, 16.626 at 25 degrees C.
candidate_facts.pattern_locator: Table 14, printed p. 30 / PDF p. 34: 1953 Swanson and Tatge powder-pattern column at 26 degrees C.
candidate_facts.composition: Tantalum, body-centered cubic. The supplied spectrographic analysis indicated faint traces of Nb, Al, Si, Fe and Mn. Dissolved gases broadened the initial diffraction peaks, and TaH produced extra lines; after the specified vacuum anneal only traces of hydride remained.
candidate_facts.processing: Annealed at 1500 degrees C in vacuum for 30 minutes in a tantalum boat; diffraction lines became sharp, with only traces of hydride remaining.
candidate_facts.purity_limit: No numeric total purity or absence of hydride is asserted; the density belongs to the selected tantalum lattice, not a directly weighed mixed specimen.

candidate_facts.name: Platinum
candidate_facts.sample: Sample prepared by the NBS Chemistry Division
candidate_facts.sample_locator: Section 2.14 Platinum (Cubic), printed p. 31 / PDF p. 35: NBS Chemistry Division sample, spectroscopic purity estimate and face-centered cubic structure.
candidate_facts.density_locator: Section 2.14, printed p. 31 / PDF p. 35, lower right: density based on the NBS lattice constant, 21.472 at 25 degrees C.
candidate_facts.pattern_locator: Table 15, printed p. 32 / PDF p. 36: 1953 Swanson and Tatge powder-pattern column at 26 degrees C.
candidate_facts.composition: Platinum, face-centered cubic. The NBS Spectroscopic Laboratory estimated the sample purity at greater than 99.99 percent.
candidate_facts.purity_limit: The greater-than purity is an estimate, not a certified grade; no unreported mass/atom-percent basis or absent-impurity claim is added.

candidate_facts.name: Gold
candidate_facts.sample: Sample purified by the NBS Chemistry Division
candidate_facts.sample_locator: Section 2.15 Gold (Cubic), printed p. 33 / PDF p. 37: NBS-purified sample, spectrographic impurities, approximate gold purity and face-centered cubic structure.
candidate_facts.density_locator: Section 2.15, printed p. 33 / PDF p. 37, right column above Table 16: density determined from the NBS lattice constant, 19.302 at 25 degrees C.

candidate_facts.purity_limit: Approximate purity and possible silver are retained; no exact purity, absent-silver assertion or unreported mass/atom-percent basis is inferred.

candidate_facts.name: Lead

candidate_facts.sample_locator: Section 2.16 Lead (Cubic), printed p. 34 / PDF p. 38: American Smelting and Refining Company sample, NBS spectrographic impurities, qualified purity, annealing and face-centered cubic structure.
candidate_facts.density_locator: Section 2.16, printed p. 34 / PDF p. 38, lower right: density based on the NBS unit-cell determination, 11.341 at 25 degrees C.

candidate_facts.purity_limit: The source's believed-greater-than qualification is retained; this is not certified purity or a mass/atom-percent assignment.

source_reuse.basis: Reuse the existing scoped NIST employee-authored government-work rights rationale and attribution for the selected NBS facts; exclude third-party comparison content. No new license audit or independent legal certification is claimed.
